newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rally on low CPI, Nasdaq gains.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rally on low CPI, Nasdaq gains.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher across the board following Friday's release of a consumer price index (CPI) that was at the low end of expectations and the rise of Israeli shares on Nasdaq late last week, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 2.89 percent, or 5.48 points, to 195.10 on an all-share turnover of 90 million shekels against 50 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Jewish New Year holiday.
The Maof 25 index rose 2.69 percent to 204.17.
"The market was reacting in a very positive way to the low CPI. Investors expect the Bank of Israel will lower interest rates by 0.5-0.7 percentage points," said Izik Winish at Capital Securities.
Israel's CPI rose 0.4 percent in August following a 0.3 percent rise in July.

"We predict the positive trend will continue. The market could have gained more than three percent today but foreign investors were selling shares because of fears over the tension along the northern border," he said.

Israel is closely watching Syrian troop movements in Lebanon and Syria. Syrian troops left a number of positions in the central Lebanese mountains last month. But Lebanese sources said this was a defensive redeployment after apparent Israeli threats to attack Syrian forces in Lebanon.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries surged 5.75 percent to 130,487 on volume of 5.8 million shekels. Lehman Brothers reiterated a 1-buy recommendation for Teva after the company received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for clonazepam, a generic equivalent of Roche's Klonopin, indicated for the treatment of seizure disorders.
Teva's share traded on Nasdaq jumped 8.2 percent on Thursday.
"The market was rising because of the low CPI. The central bank will have to lower interest rates by at least 0.5 percentage point," said a trader at Lehava Investements.
"The rise of Israeli shares traded in New York is also good for the market but it's difficult to predict how it (the Israeli market) will behave in the near future," he added.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which gained 0.75 percent to 461 on volume of 8.0 million shekels; Koor Industries, which rose 2.75 percent to 28,438 on turnover of 7.2 million shekels; and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which gained 3.75 percent to 803 on volume of 6.8 million shekels.
